title: Regular expression built from a non-literal (javascript)
description: Code in javascript constructs a RegExp from a runtime value. Attacker-chosen patterns can contain nested quantifiers that backtrack exponentially, so one request can occupy the event loop. This lexical rule flags the construction; the reviewer confirms the source is fixed or switches to a literal regex or a vetted pattern table.
remediation: Use a literal regular expression, or select from a vetted pattern table, or run user patterns through a linear-time engine such as RE2.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: flags any non-literal RegExp argument. Whether the value is attacker-controlled is not analysed.

tests.line: # audit: const re = new RegExp(req.query.q); present
